question: Which short-lived king am I?
reference: 2 Samuel 2-4 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Ish-bosheth')

clues: After my father and brothers died in one battle, my father's army chief made me king.
I ruled the northern tribes from Mahanaim, east of the Jordan, for two years.
I accused that army chief of taking one of my father's concubines, and he abandoned me for my rival.
Two of my own officers killed me on my bed and carried my head to Hebron.

question: Which bodyguard am I?
reference: 2 Samuel 23:20-23; 1 Kings 2 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Benaiah No. 1')

clues: I was the son of a priest and I commanded David's foreign guard.
On a snowy day I climbed down into a pit and killed a lion.
I struck down a huge Egyptian, wrenching away his spear and killing him with it.
Solomon made me chief of the army after I carried out the execution of Joab at the altar.

question: Which man who cursed a king am I?
reference: 2 Samuel 16:5-13; 1 Kings 2:36-46 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Shimei No. 3')

clues: As the king fled his capital during a revolt, I walked along the ridge pelting him with stones and dirt.
I called him a man of bloodshed and said God was paying him back for taking the throne.
One of his officers wanted to cut off my head, but the king spared me.
Years later the new king confined me to the city, and I was executed when I left it to chase runaway slaves.

question: Which royal counselor am I?
reference: 2 Samuel 15-17 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Ahithophel')

clues: My advice was so trusted that people treated it like a word from God.
I threw my support behind Absalom's revolt against David.
I urged Absalom to let me chase David down that very night with twelve thousand men.
When a rival's counsel was chosen instead, I went home, put my affairs in order, and hanged myself.

question: Which informer am I?
reference: 1 Samuel 21-22 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Doeg')

clues: I was an Edomite, the chief of King Saul's herdsmen.
I was present when the priest Ahimelech gave David bread and the sword of Goliath.
I reported what I had seen to the king.
When his soldiers refused the order, I myself killed eighty-five priests and put their town to the sword.

question: Which long-reigning king of Judah am I?
reference: 1 Kings 15; 2 Chronicles 14-16 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Asa')

clues: I removed my own grandmother from being queen mother because she had made a disgusting idol.
I trusted God to defeat an Ethiopian army of a million men.
But near the end, when Syria threatened, I bought off an ally and turned to physicians rather than to God.
I reigned forty-one years and was diseased in my feet at the last.

question: Which ally of Ahab am I?
reference: 1 Kings 22; 2 Chronicles 18-20 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jehoshaphat No. 1')

clues: I was a good king of Judah, but I married my son to the daughter of the king of Israel.
I went with that king to Ramoth-gilead and was nearly killed when the enemy mistook me for him.
When three nations invaded, I put singers in front of the army, and the invaders destroyed one another.
My fleet of trading ships was wrecked in port before it could sail.

question: Which rescued prince am I?
reference: 2 Kings 11-12; 2 Chronicles 24 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jehoash No. 1')

clues: I was the only child of the royal line to survive when my grandmother slaughtered the rest.
The high priest Jehoiada hid me inside the temple for six years.
At seven years old I was crowned, and the usurping queen was put to death.
I repaired the temple, but after Jehoiada died I turned away and had his son killed.

question: Which hospitable woman am I?
reference: 2 Kings 4:8-37 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Shunammite')

clues: My husband and I built a small roof chamber for a prophet who often passed our way.
The prophet told me I would hold a son in my arms within a year, and I did.
Years later the boy collapsed with head pain in the harvest field and died, and I rode hard to find the prophet.
He came, stretched himself over the child, and the boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.

question: Which prophet of the locust plague am I?
reference: Joel 1-2; Acts 2:16-21 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Joel, Book Of')

clues: I described wave after wave of locusts stripping the land bare as a picture of an invading army.
I urged the nation to declare a fast and gather at the temple to weep.
I foretold that God would pour out his spirit on all sorts of people, so that sons and daughters would prophesy.
Peter quoted my words to the crowd on the day of Pentecost.

question: Which questioning prophet am I?
reference: Habakkuk 1-3 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Habakkuk, Book Of')

clues: I complained to God that he was doing nothing about the violence and injustice all around me.
God answered that he would raise up the ruthless Chaldeans to carry out the punishment.
That troubled me more: how could a pure God use a nation even worse than the one being judged?
I ended by saying that even if every crop failed, I would still rejoice in the God of my salvation.

question: Which prophet of the temple rebuilding am I?
reference: Haggai 1-2; Ezra 5:1 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Haggai, Book Of')

clues: I rebuked the returned exiles for living in finished, paneled houses while God's house lay in ruins.
I asked whether it seemed to them that their wages went straight into a bag full of holes.
I stirred up the governor and the high priest to take up the work again.
Within a few weeks of my first message, the building of the temple resumed.

question: Which prophet of visions am I?
reference: Zechariah 1-9; 11 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Zechariah, Book Of')

clues: I worked alongside Haggai to encourage the rebuilding of the temple.
In a single night I received eight symbolic visions, including a golden lampstand and a flying scroll.
I foretold a king coming to Jerusalem humble and riding on a donkey.
I spoke of one who would be pierced, and of thirty pieces of silver thrown to the potter.

question: Which prophet of the shortest book am I?
reference: Obadiah 1-21 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Obadiah, Book Of')

clues: My book is the shortest in the Hebrew Scriptures, just one chapter long.
My whole message is a judgment against the nation of Edom.
I condemned Edom for standing by and gloating, even joining the looting, when Jerusalem fell.
I said that though Edom nested high among the rocks like an eagle, God would bring it down.

question: Which prophet against Nineveh am I?
reference: Nahum 1-3 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Nahum, Book Of')

clues: About a century after Nineveh had repented at another prophet's warning, I foretold its total ruin.
I called it a city of bloodshed, full of lies and plunder.
I pictured chariots racing madly through its streets on the night of its fall.
I said its river gates would be thrown open and its palace would melt away.

question: Which prophet of the day of Jehovah am I?
reference: Zephaniah 1-3 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Zephaniah, Book Of')

clues: I prophesied in Judah in the days of King Josiah, and I was descended from royalty.
I warned of a great and bitter day of Jehovah, near and rushing in fast.
I condemned those who told themselves that God would do nothing, either good or bad.
I closed with a promise that God would gather and restore a humble remnant.
